sections.html:
Down in the Willamette Valley, Benton County spans 679 square miles. Corvallis is where the county government sits, and it is also the largest town. Adair Village, Monroe and Philomath are the other towns, and a sliver of Albany reaches in from Linn County.

Oregon State University drives the local economy, with help from agriculture, forest products, electronics and wineries. Fall 2024 enrollment reached 37,900 students, 24,900 of them in Corvallis. Many houses near campus belong to landlords, estates or relatives living elsewhere, so tenants and distant heirs come up often in sales.

Corvallis sees 42.71 inches of precipitation a year, mostly as winter rain. Months of damp hit the same spots on most houses: roof surface and gutters, crawl space moisture, siding and decks, and grading around the foundation. Buyer inspectors check them first.

In fiscal 2024-25, about $198.5 million in tax was imposed on $11.13 billion of assessed value. The county's average rate was $17.83 per $1,000, and its Measure 5 rate was $9.45 per $1,000 of Measure 5 value.

Tax eventTiming
Statements mailedBy October 25
Payments dueFirst on November 15, then February 15, then May 15
Appeal petition deadlineDecember 31, or the Monday after when it falls on a weekend
Appeal hearingsOpens first Monday in February, closes April 15

For a bill or a payment question, ring the Tax Office on 541-766-6808. For value questions, phone Assessment at 541-766-6855.

Each property gets a real market value from the Assessor. The tax is figured on whichever is lower: that value or the maximum assessed value. The maximum began at 1995-96 values minus 10%. Growth is limited to 3% a year, along with any value added by new improvements.

A sale does not reset the maximum, which is why neighbors in matching houses can pay very different amounts. Rates apply per $1,000 of assessed value and differ by taxing district; the districts set them, not the Assessor.

Measure 5 puts a ceiling on any one account: education taxes may not pass $5 per $1,000 of real market value, nor general government taxes $10 per $1,000. If a bill exceeds it, the amount is cut back. That cut is called compression. Compression applies only where a bill actually passes the cap.

sections.h2: Due dates and where to pay
sections.html:
One payment on November 15 covers everything, or you can split it into three: that same day, then mid-February, then mid-May. Only the single November payment earns the 3% discount. When the 15th is a Saturday or Sunday, payment is due the next business day. Overdue money collects 1.333% interest on the 16th of every month.

  • Drop box outside the Kalapuya Building (4500 SW Research Way in Corvallis).
  • In person at the Tax Office, first floor of that building.
  • Mailed with your coupon to the county's post office box 964 in Corvallis, ZIP 97339.
  • Through the county website, using a card or an e-check.
  • Phone line: 1-866-898-2918.

Real property tax still unpaid after May 15 is delinquent, and foreclosure becomes possible when the first delinquency reaches three years. The Tax Department moves in this order:

  • Delinquency notices mail after May 15, and interest keeps running.
  • A courtesy notice after June 15 gives payment dates that keep a property off the published list.
  • A foreclosure notice follows July 15, which is also the last day for a personal check.
  • The property list runs in the local paper in mid to late August.
  • About 30 days later a general judgment is filed with the Circuit Court, and an owner who disagrees has 30 days to answer.

A granted judgment starts a two-year redemption period. Redeeming costs the judgment's taxes and interest, a 5% penalty and 9% annual interest over the judgment period, all at once, because partial payments are refused. Nobody has to move out while the clock runs. Heirs, lienholders of record and anyone with a recorded interest on the judgment date can also redeem. When no one does, the Tax Collector deeds the property to Benton County, which may auction it. ORS chapter 312 sets these rules.

Appeals are heard by the Property Value Appeals Board, called BOPTA, and you file the petition with the County Clerk. The filing period opens when statements are mailed and ends December 31, or the following business day if that is a weekend or holiday.

  • In person: County Clerk's counter, second floor at 4500 SW Research Way, closing at 5 p.m. on the last day.
  • By mail: P.O. Box 888, Corvallis, OR 97339, stamped by the last day.
  • Fax or Bopta@bentoncountyor.gov, received by midnight on the last day.

The burden is yours to show the value is wrong. Evidence that helps: an arm's-length sale roughly three to six months from January 1, a recent fee appraisal, adjusted comparable sales or repair estimates. A neighbor's lower bill is not evidence.

Hearings start the first Monday in February and wrap up by April 15. Disagree with the board's order? The next venue is the Oregon Tax Court Magistrate Division, and the clock is 30 days from mailing.

Oregon's tax year begins July 1 and ends June 30, with the lien attaching July 1. Escrow should walk you through who covers which part of this year's bill. If an older year was never paid, ask for the payoff in writing.

Older owners often run into two more topics. One is the state deferral program for seniors and people with disabilities: the state pays your county bill for you and puts a 6% lien on the house. Selling or transferring the home triggers repayment, due by August 15 of the next year, and heirs can end up responsible.

The other is the seller disclosure form. Under ORS 105.464 the form travels with a written offer, and the buyer keeps five days to back out. Court-appointed personal representatives and financial institutions that took a property in foreclosure are exempt from the full form.

You do not need to clear a delinquent balance before a cash sale. Escrow gets a written payoff, pays taxes and interest out of your proceeds, and records the deed. This helps most after a foreclosure notice, since the steps above stay in play until closing pays the account.

Ask who in the household can sign, and whether a lender or relative has a recorded interest. Phone the Tax Office for today's payoff and ask how far along the foreclosure timeline your account is. Then weigh a listing, with its repairs and waiting, against a written cash offer that settles the taxes at closing.

sections.h2: A practical checklist for Benton County sellers
sections.html:
Corvallis rentals and inherited houses make up a good share of local sales, so the paperwork questions tend to be the same ones. Work through them in order and you will know what a buyer or escrow officer is going to ask.

  • Confirm that this year's bill is paid and that no older year is hanging open. A single unpaid year changes how escrow prepares the payoff.
  • Check for a deferral lien if the owner was ever a senior or had a disability. That lien is paid off when the house sells.
  • Look at your last statement to see which taxing districts bill you, since districts differ from one address to the next.
  • If heirs are selling, confirm who has authority to sign. Court-appointed personal representatives get a lighter disclosure form, but a title company still wants proof of that appointment.

A cash buyer can usually work through most of these snags, though each one still needs a written payoff or a signature before funds move.

faqs.q: When are Benton County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Taxes are due November 15 in full, or in installments on November 15, February 15 and May 15. A full payment by November 15 earns a 3% discount, and anything unpaid after May 15 is delinquent.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal my Benton County assessment?
faqs.a: You can file from the day statements are mailed until December 31, or the next business day if that date is a weekend or holiday. Petitions go to the County Clerk, and hearings run from the first Monday in February to April 15.

faqs.q: Can Benton County foreclose on my house for unpaid taxes?
faqs.a: Yes, once the taxes have been delinquent for three years. After a general judgment, the owner has a two-year redemption period, and the county may deed and auction the property if nobody redeems.

faqs.q: What happens to a senior property tax deferral when the house sells?
faqs.a: The deferred taxes, 6% annual interest and recording costs come due after a sale or change of ownership. Payment is due by August 15 of the following year, and the lien stays until it is paid.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a Benton County property tax question?
faqs.a: For a bill or a payment question, ring the Tax Office on 541-766-6808. For value questions, phone Assessment at 541-766-6855. Both offices are open weekdays, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.
